text:
vikram: Heads-up — found a perf regression in mixed-draft routing tests. Baseline vs canary tokens/sec down ~12% when Llama-2-13b-draft is used as draft model and Mixtral-7B-final as final. Full flame profile linked. :frowning_face:
ashley: timeline? this is during steady-state generation or warmup? :thinking:
vikram: steady-state. Repro with our perf harness: `runtest --suite=mixed_draft_end2end --model-pair=llama-13b:draft,mixtral-7b:final --batch=8 --seq=512`
jules: any kernel selection differences between baseline & canary? maybe matmul/kernel flip when sequence length distribution changes.
vikram: yes. Canary changed kernel selector heuristics (fallback path for q4f16) -> we see more small-matmul kernels instead of large-tiled ones around token 128-160. Perf flame shows lots of kernel-launch overhead.
perfbot: autotest summary: 2026-01-30 11:02 UTC — mixed_draft_end2end: baseline 48.3 tokens/sec, canary 42.6 tokens/sec, error bars stable (n=10). KV hit ratio dropped from 0.91 -> 0.63.
sam: KV hit ratio drop is interesting. Might be tokenizer mismatch or RoPE offset differences causing cache invalidation between draft and final.
marta: we saw copy-on-change of KV keys when head dims mismatch across family variants — are heads/kv dims equal?
vikram: head dims are compatible (64) but RoPE scaling differs: Llama draft uses 1.0, Mixtral final uses scaled RoPE (0.98) because of our compatibility shim. That small mismatch causes key drift and eviction when we merge caches across drafts.
ashley: can we short-circuit cache merge if family != family? i.e., don't reuse KV across different families unless exact tokenizer+rope match. Safer but might increase latency.
jules: proposal: add a fast hash check at routing time: hash = sha1(model_family + tokenizer_id + rope_scale + head_dim) -> only reuse KV if equal. Quick to evaluate.
vikram: I already ran a quick patch on the runtime that adds the check and avoids merging when mismatch: results -> tokens/sec 47.8 (back near baseline) but increased memory churn by ~4% because more cache misses.
marta: tradeoff acceptable if it avoids correctness/perf regressions. Could also fallback to speculative decoding acceptance tuning to reduce wasted drafts.
sam: good point — acceptance rate currently at 0.5 for this workload. If we raise to 0.75 we reduce final-decoding switches, less cache churn, but higher chance of returning draft output. Need to balance QA.
ashley: can we also tweak batching heuristics to avoid kernel flips? e.g., prefer grouping by seq-length buckets, and prefer kernel consistent batches for the next N tokens?
jules: added a quick pseudo-config idea: ```batching: { seq_buckets: [64,128,256,512], prefer_kernel_stability: true, kernel_stability_window: 3 }``` Might reduce small-kernel thrash.
perfbot: profiling snippet (canary): ```GPU kernels: small_matmul_launches: 14.7k, tiled_matmul_launches: 3.2k, avg_kernel_latency: 1.8ms``` Baseline: small 6.1k, tiled 10.5k, avg 1.2ms.
vikram: also saw tokenization mismatch: Llama draft uses byte-level splits for some emoji sequences vs Mixtral splices differently -> leads to draft acceptance failing more often and triggering extra final decodes. That ties into acceptance tuning.
marta: short-term steps: 1) deploy KV-hash guard to avoid cross-family reuse 2) raise acceptance_rate to 0.7 for affected routes 3) enable kernel_stability flag in canary 4) collect new perf runs and compare
sam: agree. Also schedule an offline compaction job for KV cache to reclaim churned buffers.
ashley: longer term: consider canonicalizing tokenizer on the serving path (normalize to a shared tokenizer for paired families) or run tokenizer-compatibility checks during model onboarding and reject incompatible pairings.
jules: I'll open a PR with the kernel_stability toggle and a benchmark harness change to log per-batch kernel selection counts.
vikram: thanks. I'll push the KV-hash guard to a feature branch and run the perf suite overnight. Dropping logs in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
perfbot: created perf run 2026-01-30T11:05Z -> link: http://perf.internal/runs/2339 (will post results)
marta: nice. If overnight results look good, we can roll the KV guard and batching flag to canary and monitor token/sec + kv_hit ratio.
sam: reminder: update runbooks on how to interpret acceptance_rate regressions for product. Last time it caused visible hallucination in some flows.
vikram: acknowledged. Will coordinate with product QA before raising acceptance for public routes.
ashley: cool — looks actionable. thanks team.
